### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via last_7_days (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), this_month (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via last_30_days (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS))_
- `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`  _(via last_30_days (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), last_7_days (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), last_90_days (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), last_month (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), last_quarter (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), last_week (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), last_year (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), next_30_days (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), next_month (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), next_quarter (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), this_month (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), this_quarter (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), this_week (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), this_year (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), defaultRange (literal, a string literal in sections))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via next_30_days (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), next_month (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS), next_quarter (symbol, a field of const object DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9be17415955fdcdb2eee8d19f213c380229fadc2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `98b6feb65c479d7a31f7917dd011061c4ec08500` — the merge of head `fa259cf5cbf23a2ef2cd63be946fad1969e27f0b` into base `9be17415955fdcdb2eee8d19f213c380229fadc2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 98b6feb65c479d7a31f7917dd011061c4ec08500 && git checkout 98b6feb65c479d7a31f7917dd011061c4ec08500
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9be17415955fdcdb2eee8d19f213c380229fadc2 fa259cf5cbf23a2ef2cd63be946fad1969e27f0b && git checkout -B drift-repro 9be17415955fdcdb2eee8d19f213c380229fadc2 && git merge --no-ff fa259cf5cbf23a2ef2cd63be946fad1969e27f0b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9be17415955fdcdb2eee8d19f213c380229fadc2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9be17415955fdcdb2eee8d19f213c380229fadc2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fa259cf5cbf23a2ef2cd63be946fad1969e27f0b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/report.form.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/report-schema.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ReportDefaultInspector.tsx

Inputs read: card #36835 (body, triage 7120991703, claim 7126190576, os-dev-report 7129145144; no ruling and no earlier record on the thread), PR #36928 (body, six files, net diff against `main`), and the 69 check-runs on this head (59 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure). The remainder of the diff (two test files, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `report.dateRange.defaultRange`: unchanged. Right.** `report.zod.ts:704` still reads `z.enum(DATE_RANGE_DEFAULT_RANGES).default('this_month')`; the diff touches no `*.zod.ts`. The form row gains `type: 'select'` and `options`, and the option values are `DATE_RANGE_DEFAULT_RANGES.map(...)`, so the offered set is the enum itself, in its order, by construction.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec`: unchanged. Right.** `DEFAULT_PERIOD_LABELS` is module-private; `reportForm` is the same export with one row carrying more display data. The diff moves nothing under `packages/spec/api-surface/`, `export-origins/`, `liveness/` or `sdui.manifest.json`, and `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green on the head.
- **Generated form bundles: no move owed. Right.** `en.metadata-forms.generated.ts:2288` carries `label` (and the hint) per form row and nothing per option; the row's label and hint are unchanged, and `i18n-bundle-extract.ts` has no option-name emitter. No forms baseline or generated artefact in the tree holds a form row's options.
- **Rendered option set in Studio: same 17 values, same leading unset item. Right.** `SchemaForm.tsx:2447` gives `fieldSpec.options` precedence over `schema.enum`; both branches share `offerUnset` and the same `value`/`onValueChange` wiring, so only the item text moves.
- **New app-shell exports `defaultPeriodLabelKey` and `withDefaultPeriodLabels`:** internal to a private package (`"private": true`), one consumer in the diff. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — holds. Nothing an author can write, and nothing a validator accepts or refuses, differs at this head.
Metadata-protocol: none — holds. No protocol step, no migration entry, no schema key.

Changeset `.changeset/36835-report-default-period-labels.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch and `@object-ui/app-shell` patch. Patch matches what the diff publishes (display names on one form row of a published const; a private package named for the record). Both lines are on the PR body and the changeset alike. `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation (3), PR body cites readings at `baead759`: verified in the tree. `git diff baead759 fa259cf5` is one added line, `readOnly={false}`, in the new inspector test. No reviewed file differs between the two heads, and the head's own check-runs cover it.
- Deviations (1), (2), (4) are process notes with no effect on the tree.
- Out-of-scope finding, dashboard sibling (`dashboard.form.ts` declares no `dateRange` children, so its select still lists raw presets): confirmed outside this card's file surface; it is the seat's to file, not a defect of this diff.
- Out-of-scope note, no option-name slot in `metadataForms`: confirmed by reading (`metadata-form-i18n.ts` overlays label, helpText, placeholder). It bounds this fix to the Studio inspector for zh; other spec forms that already declare `type: 'select'` with English `options` (`field.form.ts`, `hook.form.ts`, `object.form.ts`) sit in the same state on `main`, so this row follows precedent.
- Base drift: `main` moved from the merge base `b3d953e7` to `49c6bf3d`; none of the three reviewed files nor `data/date-range-presets.ts` changed in between.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, id materialisation or join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/report.form.ts`**

- Option list against the enum, now and later: derived, not hand-listed. Values come from `DATE_RANGE_DEFAULT_RANGES.map`; names come from a `Record` keyed by `DateRangeDefaultRange`, so a preset added to `data/date-range-presets.ts` (or to the `custom` tail in `dashboard.zod.ts:1474`) is a compile error here until named, and a stale key is an excess-property error. The jsdoc sentence saying so is true.
- English names against the runtime windows (`date-range-presets.ts:23-38`): all 16 presets read correctly (calendar windows for this/last/next week, month, quarter, year; rolling windows for last 7/30/90 and next 30 days). `custom` resolves to no window (`ReportDateRange.tsx:95`), which the jsdoc states.
- English names against the cited console rows: all 17 equal `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` `dashboard.filters.range.*` (16) and `dashboard.filters.custom`, character for character including the ellipsis. The jsdoc claim holds at this head.
- `type: 'select'` plus `options` on a composite child is the established spelling in spec forms and parses through `defineForm`; `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` are green.
- A stored value outside the list: the list equals the schema enum, so any such value is one the schema already refuses. The select shows an empty trigger for it and writes nothing until the author picks, the same as the enum fallback did before. No regression.

**`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/report-schema.ts`**

- `defaultPeriodLabelKey` agrees with the chip it cites: `ReportDateRange.tsx:211` reads `dashboard.filters.range.PRESET`, `:219` and `:242` read `dashboard.filters.custom`.
- `withDefaultPeriodLabels` does what its jsdoc says: returns the same form when no `dateRange.defaultRange` options exist, otherwise copies only form, section, `dateRange` row and the child. It does not mutate the cached localized form from `getReportForm`.
- zh names against the console's own text: `zh-Hans.ts:2069-2087` holds all 16 range rows plus `custom: '自定义…'`; they are the rows the chip renders, so builder and viewer read the same words. No new string is added anywhere in the diff.

**`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ReportDefaultInspector.tsx`**

- The zh gate (`isZhLocale(locale)`) matches the comment above it. A missing pack row falls back to the spec's English name through `defaultValue: authored`, never to the raw preset or the key. A designer locale of zh with the app language in English reads the en pack, which equals the spec names; zh-Hant reads its own pack, which carries the rows.
- `appT` in the memo's dependency list is sound: `useObjectTranslation` returns a memoised `t` bound to `boundT`, and the hook subscribes to store writes (`STORE_WRITES_RERENDER`), as the comment says. Not re-measured against react-i18next's source, which is not installed here; `Test UI` and `Live E2E UI` are green on the head.

Findings:

- N1 (nit) — the gate is zh-only although the console packs carry `dashboard.filters.range.*` for the other shipped locales too; a ja or de designer keeps English names. This matches the rest of the panel and the card's en plus zh-CN acceptance. Left as an accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit) — `Custom…` keeps the chip's trailing ellipsis in a settings select where choosing it opens nothing. It is deliberate parity with the chip and pinned by the parity case. Left as an accepted deviation.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#3 · head fa259cf5 · 2026-11-24T10:48Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: `fa259cf5cbf23a2ef2cd63be946fad1969e27f0b`
Reviewer: L1-b (seat 3, area ux-D). Contract review: L2 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS on this head, comment 7129263701 (claim 7129189093), nits only.
Tier: not Tier H. This is card #36835's only PR, 6 files, 323 changed lines. `check-governed-merges --pr 36928`: not governed.

### Read
- Net diff `origin/main...fa259cf5`, the PR body, card #36835 with claim 7126190576 and dev report 7129145144.
- Check-runs on `fa259cf5`: 59 success, 10 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. `l1-face.mjs --pr 36928`: CLEAN, 13 items, none flagged.
- The PR body cites readings at `baead759`. The only change from there to `fa259cf5` is `readOnly={false}` in the new inspector test, so the readings still hold.

### Checklist
- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #36835`.
- **Scope.** The files are `report.form.ts`, `report-schema.ts`, `ReportDefaultInspector.tsx`, two tests and a changeset. All are inside the claim surface.
- **Options follow the preset table.** The options come from `DATE_RANGE_DEFAULT_RANGES.map(...)`, and the names from a `Record<DateRangeDefaultRange, string>`. If a preset is added later, the build fails until it is named. Stored values, the default and the schema enum are unchanged.
- **zh names.** `withDefaultPeriodLabels` renames the options through `dashboard.filters.range.*` and `dashboard.filters.custom`. These are the rows the report page's period chip reads. `zh-Hans.ts` and `zh-Hant.ts` carry all sixteen range rows plus `自定义…` / `自定義…`. A missing row falls back to the spec's English name through `defaultValue`, never to the raw preset. No new strings, so no catalogue rows are owed.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/spec` and `@object-ui/app-shell` patch, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. That is right: only the form's option names move. The L2 confirms the authorable surface, api-surface and generated metadata-form rows are unchanged.
- **Card acceptance.**
  - The select shows named options in en and zh-CN: met. The inspector test opens the select in both languages. It asserts that no stored preset shows, and it uses the row's own zh label as a positive control.
  - The report form's `defaultRange` options carry names: met. A test pins the spec names equal to the en pack rows, one for one.

### Findings
No must-fix, no should-fix.

- **N1 (nit).** In the zh case of the inspector test, `await waitFor(() => expect(offered).toContain('本季度'))` waits on an array that has already been captured, so it retries nothing. The assertion is still real: the options are read after the list opens, and CI is green. A later edit could re-read the options inside the `waitFor`.
- **N2 (nit).** The zh switch is decided by the designer `locale` (`isZhLocale`), but the names come from the app's `t`. The two only differ when the designer locale and the app language differ. In that case the names come from the en pack, which is the spec's English, so nothing breaks.
- The L2 record's N1 (other designer locales keep English) and N2 (`Custom…` keeps the chip's ellipsis) are adopted as nits.

### Note to the seat
- Not Tier H, not governed, both reviews pass, so the seat can land this through the relay. `Fixes #36835` closes the card at merge.
- From the L2: `dashboard.form.ts` declares no `dateRange` children, so the dashboard's Default Period select still lists raw presets. This is the same defect on the sibling form, outside this card. File it if wanted.
